subject.title: Skipped group messages behind requireMention do not reach message hooks, which blocks full-history archive plugins

question: Should OpenClaw expose mention-skipped/pre-session inbound content to trusted installed plugins through a public read-only hook, and must that hook be explicitly gated before release?
rationale: The requested API changes the Plugin SDK privacy boundary by allowing plugins to observe content before current mention/session dispatch gates expose it publicly.

options.title: Gate The Public Hook Before Landing
options.body: Add an explicit operator/plugin permission or access gate, document the payload boundary, and land the hook only after that contract is visible.

options.title: Approve Installed-Plugin Trust
options.body: Accept that any installed plugin registering the hook may observe skipped inbound content without an extra gate, and document that security model clearly.

options.title: Keep Internal Ingest Only
options.body: Pause or reject the public hook and leave full-fidelity archive plugins dependent on internal or channel-specific integrations for now.

recommendation.title: Gate The Public Hook Before Landing
recommendation.body: Add an explicit operator/plugin permission or access gate, document the payload boundary, and land the hook only after that contract is visible.

likelyOwner.reason: They authored the current internal skipped-message ingest path and are the clearest history owner for deciding whether that boundary should become public.
